## Overview

A button starts an action: search flights, continue to payment, apply a coupon, cancel a booking. It is a label with an optional glyph on either side and an optional spinner. A button does something on the current screen or moves the user forward in a flow. Going to another place, such as "See all offers", is a link's job unless the link sits where a button is expected, for example at the end of a card.

The set is **Button** (`58:202`) on the Button page. It has 240 variants across five axes:

- **Hierarchy** sets how much attention the action asks for: Primary, Secondary, Tertiary or Text.
- **Intent** is Default or Destructive. Destructive turns every hierarchy red for an action that deletes or cancels something that cannot be undone.
- **Size** is Large (48), Medium (40) or Small (32). Size changes height, padding, radius, glyphs and type together.
- **State** covers Default, Hover, Pressed, Focus and Disabled.
- **Surface** is Default or Inverse. Inverse is for buttons on dark sections: hero banners, navy offer cards, dark tooltips and snackbars, and photos under a scrim.

### Choosing a hierarchy

| Hierarchy | Looks like | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary** | Solid brand fill, white label | The one action the screen exists for: Search, Continue, Pay now, Book. One per screen, sheet or dialog. |
| **Secondary** | Brand outline, no fill | The alternative to a Primary, next to it: Modify search beside Search, Add traveller beside Continue. |
| **Tertiary** | Light brand tint, no outline | A supporting action that still needs a visible target, often several in a row: Apply on a coupon, Add-ons on a fare card, a group of filters. |
| **Text** | Label only | Low-emphasis or inline actions where space is tight: Skip, View details, Edit, Cancel in a dialog. |

- **One Primary per view.** Two solid buttons compete. When two actions carry equal weight, make one Primary and the other Secondary, and put the Primary last in the reading order (right of the pair, or below it in a stack).
- **Destructive is for consequences, not for emphasis.** Use it only when the action deletes data, cancels a booking or forfeits money. Use the hierarchy the action would have had otherwise: a Primary destructive button in a confirmation dialog, a Text destructive button for Remove in a list. Do not use red to make an ordinary action louder.
- **Size follows the context, not the importance.** Large for the main action of a mobile flow, such as a sticky bottom bar. Medium is the default in content and on web. Small is for dense rows, cards and tables, on web or with extra hit area (see Accessibility).
- **Inverse follows the background.** Set Surface to Inverse whenever the button sits on a dark section. Never place a Default-surface button on a dark background.

### When to use something else

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| Turning a setting on or off | Switch |
| Picking one of a few options that stay visible | Segmented control or Chip |
| Filtering a list | Chip |
| Several related actions behind one control | A Button that opens a Menu |
| Moving to another page inside running text | An inline link (`text-link`), not a Text button |
| Telling the user an action happened, with Undo | Snackbar, whose action is its own control |

### Composition

- **Container**: the fill, the outline (Secondary only) and the corner radius.
- **Content row**, centred: spinner, leading icon, label, trailing icon, in that order. Only the label is always present.
- **Focus ring**: a separate rounded rectangle 4 px outside the container, shown only on keyboard focus.
- **Tint** (Inverse only): a layer whose opacity binds a `button/bg-opacity-*` token, for the translucent inverse fills.

## API

| Property | Figma | Code (`Button`) | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Label | `Label` text | `label` (required) | "Label" |
| Hierarchy | `Hierarchy` variant | `hierarchy`: `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `text` | Primary |
| Intent | `Intent` variant | `intent`: `default`, `destructive` | Default |
| Size | `Size` variant | `size`: `small`, `medium`, `large` | Medium |
| Surface | `Surface` variant | `surface`: `default`, `inverse` | Default |
| Leading icon | `Show Leading Icon` + `Select Leading Icon` swap | `leadingIcon` (an icon name; omit to hide) | off; Icon / plus |
| Trailing icon | `Show Trailing Icon` + `Select Trailing Icon` swap | `trailingIcon` (an icon name; omit to hide) | off; Icon / chevron-right |
| Loading | `Show Loading` | `isLoading` | off |
| Disabled | `State=Disabled` | `isDisabled` | enabled |

The code component also passes through native button attributes such as `onClick`, `type` (default `button`) and `aria-*`.

### Figma-only properties

- **State Hover, Pressed and Focus** exist for mocks. In code they are `:hover` (pointer devices only), `:active` and `:focus-visible`. Only Disabled is a prop.
- **The spinner glyph is fixed** to Icon / spinner and has no swap property.
- **The Tint layer** is hidden on the Default surface and has no property of its own.

### Examples

| Pattern | Setup |
|---|---|
| Flight search | Primary, Large, "Search flights", full width in the search card |
| Review booking footer | Primary "Continue" with Secondary "Modify" beside it, Large, in a sticky bottom bar |
| Coupon row | Tertiary, Small, "Apply" |
| Fare card | Text, Medium, "View details" with trailing Icon / chevron-right |
| Payment in progress | Primary, Large, `isLoading`, "Paying" |
| Cancel booking dialog | Text "Keep booking" and Primary Destructive "Cancel booking" |
| Offer banner on navy | Primary, Surface Inverse, "Book now"; Text, Surface Inverse, "Terms apply" |

## Behaviour

- **Width.** A button hugs its content but is never narrower than `button/min-width` (86), at every size, so short labels such as "OK" or "Apply" still make a usable target. One shared minimum also means a button that has been stretched keeps its width when its size changes. Long labels grow the button. It can also fill its container, for example a full-width bottom bar; the content stays centred.
- **Label.** One line, never wrapped and never truncated. Keep it to one to three words, starting with a verb: "Search flights", not "Click here to search".
- **Icons.** The two slots are independent, so a button can show either, both or neither. Use a leading icon to clarify the action (Icon / plus for Add traveller) and a trailing chevron for an action that moves forward. Do not add an icon just to decorate.
- **Loading.** The spinner appears ahead of everything else, including the leading icon, and the label stays. Change the label to a present participle where it helps ("Paying"), so the button does not jump in width more than needed. The spinner turns once every `button/spinner-duration` (800 ms) at constant speed; under reduced motion it turns three times slower instead of stopping, so the button still reads as busy.
- **Loading does not block taps in code.** `isLoading` sets `aria-busy` but leaves the button active. The screen must ignore repeated taps while the work runs, so a payment is not sent twice.
- **Disabled wins over Loading.** A disabled button never shows that it is busy to assistive technology, even if `isLoading` is set.
- **Prefer an enabled button with an error over a disabled one.** A disabled Continue does not say what is missing. Keep it enabled and show the missing field's error on tap, unless the action is truly unavailable (sold out, past the cut-off time).
- **Hover** applies to pointer devices only. On touch screens the pressed state is the feedback.

## Structure

### Anatomy

| # | Part | Layer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Container | the variant root | Fill, inside outline, radius |
| 2 | Tint | `Tint` | Inverse only, hidden elsewhere |
| 3 | Focus ring | `Focus Ring` | Focus only, 4 px outside the container |
| 4 | Spinner | `Spinner` (Icon / spinner) | Optional |
| 5 | Leading icon | `Icon Leading` (Icon / plus by default) | Optional |
| 6 | Label | `Label` | Always shown |
| 7 | Trailing icon | `Icon Trailing` (Icon / chevron-right by default) | Optional |

### Dimensions

| Measure | Token | Large | Medium | Small |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum height | `button/min-height-*` | 48 | 40 | 32 |
| Minimum width | `button/min-width` | 86 | 86 | 86 |
| Vertical padding | `button/padding-y-*` | 12 | 8 | 4 |
| Horizontal padding | `button/padding-x-*` | 20 | 16 | 12 |
| Gap between content | `button/gap-sm` | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| Icon and spinner size | `button/icon-size-*` | 24 | 20 | 16 |
| Corner radius | `button/radius-*` | 12 (`lg`) | 8 (`md`) | 8 (`md`) |
| Label type | `label/*/bold` | 16/24 | 14/20 | 12/16 |
| Outline (Secondary) | `button/border-width` | 1, inside | 1, inside | 1, inside |
| Focus ring width | `button/focus-ring-width` | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Focus ring gap | `button/focus-ring-offset` | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Focus ring radius | `button/radius-xl` / `button/radius-lg` | 16 | 12 | 12 |

- **Every hierarchy has the same footprint.** Only Secondary paints an outline, and it is drawn inside the container, so a Secondary button is exactly as big as a Primary one. The other hierarchies have the 1 px stroke configured but transparent; do not build a border from it.
- **Icons match the label line height** (24, 20, 16), so glyphs and text share one centre line.
- **The focus ring** sits 4 px outside the container on every side: a 2 px gap, then the 2 px ring. Its radius is the button radius plus 4, so it stays concentric with the corner.
- **The label is in bold** at every size and in every hierarchy. In myBiz and Goibibo it follows the brand typeface and `weight.bold`.
- **Web optical centring.** Browsers draw 12 px Lato half a pixel higher and 14 px Lato half a pixel lower than Figma, so the Small and Medium labels shift by a quarter of `space-3xs`. 16 px text matches.

## Color

Every colour binds a `button/*` token named `button/{part}-{hierarchy}[-destructive]-{state}`, where part is `bg`, `border`, `label` or `icon` and state is `default`, `hover`, `pressed` or `disabled`. The tables give the semantic token each one points to and its MakeMyTrip value. Focus has no colour state of its own: a focused button keeps its resting colours and adds the ring.

| Label and icons, destructive | `text-` / `icon-warning` #C10007 | `*-warning-on-bg-fill-subtlest-hover` #9F0712 | `*-warning-on-bg-fill-subtlest-pressed` #82181A | `text-` / `icon-disabled` #A1A1A1 |

- **Text sits one tint step lighter than Secondary and Tertiary.** Its hover fill is the Tertiary resting tint and its pressed fill is the Tertiary hover tint, so a bare label does not jump to a heavy block when pressed.
- **Labels darken on hover and press** in Secondary, Tertiary and Text, to stay readable on the darker tint. Primary keeps its white label in every state.
- **Labels and icons share a colour but not a token.** Each has its own `label-*` and `icon-*` key, so the two can be tuned apart.
- **Fills are `bg-fill` roles**, not `bg-surface`: a button is a control, even when it sits inside a card, snackbar or tooltip.

### Inverse surface

`surface=inverse` swaps every colour to a `button/*-inverse-*` token. The surface comes after the hierarchy in the key: `button/{part}-{hierarchy}-inverse[-destructive]-{state}`. Size and shape do not change.

- **Primary keeps the light fills** (#0088FF, destructive #C10007), so it is the same button on every surface. Only Disabled changes, to a solid #262626 fill with a #737373 label.
- **Secondary, Tertiary and Text use light brand blue.** Labels sit at step 300 (#83DFFF, destructive #FFA2A2). Icons and outlines sit one step deeper, at 400 (#48BBFF, destructive #FF6467). Hover and pressed get one step lighter each, the mirror of the light surface, where they get darker.
- **Translucent fills.** The Tertiary fill and the hover and pressed fills of Secondary and Text are a tint colour (`bg-fill-brand-inverse` #48BBFF, `bg-fill-warning-inverse` #FF6467) drawn at a `button/bg-opacity-*` token, so they work on near-black, navy and photos alike. Disabled fills stay solid (`bg-fill-inverse-disabled` #262626).
  - CSS: `color-mix(in srgb, var(--button-bg-tertiary-inverse-default) calc(var(--button-bg-opacity-tertiary-inverse-default) * 100%), transparent)`
  - SwiftUI: `.opacity()` on the fill. Compose: `.copy(alpha = …)`.
  - Figma: the `Tint` layer, whose layer opacity binds the variable.
- **Focus ring** is `button/focus-ring-inverse` (`border-brand-inverse` #48BBFF) or `button/focus-ring-inverse-destructive` (`border-warning-inverse` #FF6467). The light ring (#0088FF) reads 5.62:1 on near-black but only 3.50:1 on navy.

| Fill, destructive | `bg-fill-warning-strong` #C10007 | `bg-fill-warning-strong-hover` #E7000B | `bg-fill-warning-strong-pressed` #9F0712 | `bg-fill-inverse-disabled` #262626 |
| Label and icons (both intents) | #FFFFFF | #FFFFFF | #FFFFFF | `text-` / `icon-inverse-disabled` #737373 |

The brand blue and the myBiz and Goibibo primaries use the 3:1 floor of the azure and brand-role exceptions (README → Azure contrast exception). Every other pair meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for outlines and icons.

### Semantics

- **One focus stop.** The label is the accessible name. The icons, the spinner and the focus ring are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
- **Name the consequence.** Destructive red is not announced, so the label carries it: "Cancel booking", not a red "Cancel". An icon-only meaning never replaces the label.
- **Loading** is a state, not a new name. The name stays the label; the busy state rides on `aria-busy`, `accessibilityValue` or `stateDescription`. Keep the button in the focus order while it loads, so focus is not lost when the work ends.
- **Disabled** removes the button from the focus order and is announced as dimmed or disabled where it can be reached. It never announces that it is busy.
- **Touch target.** Large (48) clears the 44 pt iOS and 48 dp Android targets on its own. Medium (40) and Small (32) do not: give them extra hit area from the layout (padding or an invisible hit box) on touch screens, and keep 8 px between neighbouring buttons.

| Platform | Mapping |
|---|---|
| Web | A native `button type="button"` (or `submit` in a form). The visible text is the name; no `aria-label` while the label is visible. Loading sets `aria-busy="true"`. Disabled uses the native `disabled` attribute; use `aria-disabled="true"` instead when the button must stay discoverable, and reject activation in script. Icons are `aria-hidden`. The ring follows `:focus-visible`, so mouse clicks do not paint it. |
| iOS / VoiceOver | SwiftUI `Button` or `UIButton` with the label as its text. Hide the glyphs with `.accessibilityHidden(true)`. Loading sets `accessibilityValue` to "Loading" and posts an announcement once when it starts. Disabled sets `.disabled(true)`, which VoiceOver reads as dimmed. |
| Android / TalkBack | A clickable composable with `Role.Button` and `mergeDescendants`, glyphs with `contentDescription = null`. Loading sets `stateDescription = "Loading"`. Disabled sets `enabled = false`. |

---

## Platform mapping

| | Android | iOS | Web |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | A custom composable on `Surface` or `Box` with `clickable(role = Role.Button)`; Material 3 `Button` only if its shape, colours, padding and minimum size are all overridden from the tokens | `Button` with a custom `ButtonStyle` drawn from the tokens | The `Button` component in `storybook/src/components/Button` |
| Outline | `Modifier.border` inside the shape, Secondary only | `RoundedRectangle().strokeBorder`, Secondary only | An inset `box-shadow`, so the outline never adds height |
| Pressed | `interactionSource.collectIsPressedAsState()` | `configuration.isPressed` in the style | `:active` |
| Focus ring | Drawn on keyboard focus only, 2 dp gap and 2 dp ring | Shown under Full Keyboard Access focus | `outline` with `outline-offset`, on `:focus-visible` |
| Inverse tints | `color.copy(alpha = opacity)` | `.opacity(opacity)` on the fill | `color-mix()` with the opacity token |
| Spinner | `rememberInfiniteTransition` rotation, linear, 800 ms | `rotationEffect` with a linear repeating animation | CSS `animation` on `button/spinner-duration` |

---

## Known gaps

- **Medium and Small miss the touch target.** At 40 and 32 they rely on the layout for the rest of the 44 / 48 hit area (`button/min-height-md` and `-sm` say so in their descriptions).
- **`button/gap-xs`, `gap-md` and `gap-lg` are defined but unused.** The Figma component applies `gap-sm` (4) at every size, so the space between icon and label does not grow with the button. Decide whether Large should take `gap-md` (8) before using the other steps.
- **Inverse Primary pressed is 2.72:1 against near-black.** Primary hover and pressed reuse the light fills, which get darker. The white label keeps the button readable (3.52:1 at rest, 5.53:1 or more on hover and press), and the fill is a momentary state. Accepted so Primary stays one button on every surface.
- **No truncation rule.** A label longer than its container overflows rather than ending in an ellipsis. Keep labels short; there is no multi-line button.
- **No icon-only button.** A glyph without a label (close, share, favourite) needs its own component with an accessible name and a 48 hit area.
- **Loading does not block activation in code.** See Behaviour.

## Token reference

299 tokens under `component.button` in `tokens/tokens.json`, mirrored 1:1 as `button/*` in the Figma `component` collection:

| Group | Count |
|---|---|
| Fills: `bg-{hierarchy}[-destructive]-{state}`, light and inverse | 64 |
| Inverse fill opacity: `bg-opacity-*` | 14 |
| Outlines: `border-{hierarchy}[-destructive]-{state}`, light and inverse | 64 |
| Labels: `label-{hierarchy}[-destructive]-{state}`, light and inverse | 64 |
| Icons: `icon-{hierarchy}[-destructive]-{state}`, light and inverse | 64 |
| Focus ring: `focus-ring`, `focus-ring-destructive`, `focus-ring-inverse`, `focus-ring-inverse-destructive`, `focus-ring-width`, `focus-ring-offset` | 6 |
| Dimensions: `min-height-{lg,md,sm}`, `min-width`, `padding-x-{lg,md,sm}`, `padding-y-{lg,md,sm}`, `gap-{lg,md,sm,xs}`, `icon-size-{lg,md,sm}`, `radius-{xl,lg,md}`, `border-width` | 21 |
| Motion: `spinner-duration`, `spinner-easing` | 2 |

Platform names follow the standard pipeline: `button/bg-primary-hover` → `--button-bg-primary-hover` (CSS) → `buttonBgPrimaryHover` (Swift / Kotlin) → `tokens.button["bg-primary-hover"]` (TS, the default export of `dist/web/tokens.ts`). The brand colours above are brandable: on iOS read them from the `\.cosmosBrand` environment value and on Android from `LocalCosmosBrand`, not from `CosmosTokens`, so the button follows myBiz and Goibibo (README → Brands).
